hints: Look at what is common and what is rare in pond 1. Which phenotypes increase and which almost disappear when tadpole density is high and food is low?
Think about why intermediates would struggle most when food is scarce. What two specialist foods are they competing for against the two specialists?
Recall the name for selection that favours both extremes at the same time and link it to intense competition as the selection pressure.
walkthrough:
Spot the pattern in pond 1**
You see high density, low food, and mostly the two extremes with very few intermediates. That tells you the middle phenotype is losing out, while the two opposite ends are winning. Selection is pulling the population apart in two directions.

Name the type of selection**
When both extremes are favoured and the intermediate is selected against, this is disruptive selection, also called diversifying selection. Use that exact term.

Explain why with competition**
High numbers plus low food means intense intraspecific competition. Detritus feeders are specialists on detritus and algae, carnivores are specialists on fairy shrimps. Intermediates try to eat everything but are not as efficient as either specialist, so they get outcompeted for both food types and fail to survive and reproduce. Lack of food is the selection pressure.

Final answer: Disruptive / diversifying selection; extremes (detritus feeders and carnivores) are selected for / survive and intermediates are selected against; due to high / intense competition / limited food as selection pressure, intermediates are outcompeted for detritus / algae and shrimp / small animals.

hints: Compare pond 2 with pond 1. Here density is low, food is sufficient, and now the middle type is commonest. Which direction is selection pushing?
Think about diet breadth. What can intermediates eat that specialists cannot, and why does that matter less when food is plentiful?
Recall the name for selection that favours the average phenotype and removes extremes, and link it to low competition and better growth on a varied diet.
walkthrough:
Spot the opposite pattern in pond 2**
Low density plus enough food for all, and now intermediates dominate while extremes are few. The population is centred on the middle, not split apart. That is the hallmark of selection favouring the average.

Name the type of selection**
When the intermediate is favoured and both extremes are selected against, this is stabilising selection. It narrows variation around the mean.

Explain why intermediates win here**
With little competition, there is no penalty for being a generalist. Intermediates can eat detritus, algae and fairy shrimps, so they get a greater variety in the diet. That improves growth and development, while specialists are limited to a narrower food range and are selected against.

Final answer: Stabilising selection; intermediates are selected for / survive and extremes (carnivores and detritus feeders) are selected against; due to low / less competition, intermediates can eat both / all / a wider range of foods, giving improved growth and development.

hints: In pond 2 most tadpoles are intermediates with medium intestines. What symmetrical bell shape shows most individuals in the middle and few at both ends?
walkthrough:
Link continuous variation to curve shape**
Intestine length shows continuous variation because it is controlled by many genes plus environment. That always gives a smooth bell shape when you plot number against length.

Place the peak for pond 2**
In pond 2 stabilising selection favours intermediates, so the peak (highest number of tadpoles) must be in the middle of the x-axis for medium intestines, falling symmetrically to low numbers for very short and very long intestines.
Final answer: Draw a symmetrical bell-shaped normal distribution curve with peak at intermediate / medium intestine length.

hints: Start from the meaning of sympatric - same place. What must be true about geography if new species form in the same pond?
If there is no mountain or river separating them, what other type of barrier could stop the carnivores and detritus feeders interbreeding?
walkthrough:
Define the core idea**
Sympatric means in the same place. New species form from one original population without any geographical barrier, but they become reproductively isolated so they can no longer interbreed to produce fertile offspring.

Add how isolation happens**
Isolation is ecological or behavioural, for example feeding in different parts of the pond, different breeding times, different courtship, or disruptive selection favouring extremes until gene flow stops. That is different from allopatric speciation which needs geographical separation.
Final answer: Formation of new species due to reproductive isolation in the same geographical area / region; caused by ecological / behavioural separation / isolation / differences.

hints: To compare toads by DNA, what molecule would you sequence in all three species and then line up side by side?
Once sequences are aligned, what would you count to measure similarity, and how does that relate to how recently they shared an ancestor?
Look at Fig. 7.3. Which two species share the most recent branch point, and what would you expect their DNA to show?
walkthrough:
Sequence and align DNA**
Take the same gene or genome region from S. multiplicata, S. hammondii and S. bombifrons, determine the base sequence, and align them using bioinformatics software / databases such as BLAST.

Use differences as a molecular clock**
Count the number of nucleotide differences. Mutations accumulate over time, so fewer differences means less time since divergence from a common ancestor and a closer evolutionary relationship.

Apply to the tree**
Fig. 7.3 shows S. hammondii and S. bombifrons diverging about 15 million years ago, while S. multiplicata split off about 30 million years ago. So analysis would show S. hammondii and S. bombifrons have the fewest genetic differences and are most closely related.

Final answer: Obtain / compare DNA sequences for all three species; count nucleotide / base differences / similarities; fewer differences means more closely related / less time since divergence; S. hammondii and S. bombifrons are most similar / have fewest differences, shown by most recent common ancestor in Fig. 7.3.
